title: Hash maps and sets
summary: unordered_map, unordered_set and optional: the tools behind most O(n) interview solutions.
hints: `word_count`: `++counts[word];` is enough. `operator[]` inserts a default value (0 for `int`) when the key is missing, then you increment it.

`first_duplicate`: keep a `std::unordered_set<int> seen`. `seen.insert(x)` returns a pair whose `.second` is `false` if `x` was already present. Return `x` the moment that happens, and `std::nullopt` if the loop finishes.

`two_sum`: for each position `j`, look up `target - v[j]` in a map from value to index. If it is there, the answer is `{that index, j}`. Otherwise store `v[j]` in the map. `is_anagram`: count the letters of `a` up, the letters of `b` down, and check that every count ends at 0.
